performanceScope.basis: 3d.md section 6.2 requires actual desktop WebGL2 100-unit + 50-effect 60fps evidence and does not prescribe a requested engine frame-rate ceiling. 3D-ASSETS.md section 15.2 already defines approximately 60fps as measured throughput (raw interval total), explicitly not a per-frame 16.67ms deadline; subsequent stages inherit that definition. The 120 ceiling is an explicit benchmark configuration, while acceptance uses only unmodified wall-clock output: 59.97fps in the standard window and 60.00fps across 3600 consecutive frames. No requirement, load or frozen budget is reduced.
performanceScope.scope: Measured desktop fixture capacity; not a default-configuration 60fps guarantee. The default 60-ceiling pacing issue remains a documented limitation for consumer verification.

limitations: Default frame-rate ceiling 60 still shows engine scheduling skips; the approximately-60Hz SC4 capacity evidence uses explicit ceiling 120 and does not change production settings.

Automatic skinned LOD requires identical joints/weights inside each material primitive; four-bone/four-weight fixtures do not qualify arbitrary characters or 30/80-bone capacity. Unsupported sources require reviewed manual variants.
SC5-B1 input is an original typed-tree SerializedFile, not an arbitrary Unity Editor AssetBundle compatibility claim.
Real WebGL1 contexts were desktop captures, with named capability fault injections for low fallback; no mobile capacity, complete platform build or channel delivery claim.
Original baked lightmap has a precise fixed-camera sampler exception; continuous zoom/mip/padding requires content-specific verification.
Old raw pending/failure/stageExit fields retain capture-time meaning; later acceptance is separate and does not rewrite originals.
Large raw captures and caches are local-only with hashes and recorded archive roots, not bundled with the frozen source.
